1.anatomical_location: The peripheral zone forms the posterolateral outer portion of the prostate, surrounding much of the transition and central gland and lying near the prostatic capsule and rectum.
1.morphology: It is a curved, relatively thin peripheral compartment whose thickness and continuity vary from the base to the apex.
1.boundary: Its outer margin follows the prostatic capsule, while its inner interface with the transition zone can be subtle and partially indistinct.
1.neighboring_relations: It is adjacent to the transition zone medially, the capsule and periprostatic tissues laterally, the rectum posteriorly, and the neurovascular bundles posterolaterally.
1.typical_appearance: On T2-weighted MRI the normal peripheral zone is usually relatively high in signal, while suspicious tissue may be focally low in signal; on ADC maps the normal zone is usually relatively high in ADC signal, while diffusion-restricted suspicious tissue appears low in ADC signal.

2.anatomical_location: The transition zone is the central periurethral glandular compartment, located inside the peripheral zone and extending between the prostate base and apex.
2.morphology: It is a paired-to-confluent central structure with a compact rounded or ovoid contour that often becomes heterogeneous and nodular with benign prostatic hyperplasia.
2.boundary: Its pseudocapsular interface with the peripheral zone may be visible on T2-weighted MRI but can be irregular or indistinct, especially with glandular enlargement.
2.neighboring_relations: It surrounds the prostatic urethra, lies medial to the peripheral zone, inferior to the bladder neck, and anterior to the ejaculatory ducts and central gland structures.
2.typical_appearance: On T2-weighted MRI the transition zone is commonly heterogeneous with mixed high- and low-signal nodules; on ADC maps its signal is also heterogeneous, while diffusion-restricted suspicious tissue tends to show lower ADC signal than adjacent benign tissue.
